report.headline: Usage projected to fall to 18.8% from 24.9% in the EuroLeague, with the efficiency projection carrying no real signal

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 18.8% in the NBA, down from 24.9% in the 2022-23 EuroLeague season, and slightly below the NBA average of 20.1%.

risks.text: The projected NBA usage rate of 18.8% sits below the league average of 20.1%; the model does carry limited real signal here, with an out-of-fold error of 3.3% against a league-mean baseline error of 4.3%, but the margin is thin.

The true shooting projection of 58.4% carries no information: the model's out-of-fold error (4.7%) equals the trivial league-mean baseline error (4.7%), so it should not be used to judge scoring efficiency in the new league.
At 27.0 years old in the source season, and with the estimate resting on only 61 historical EL->NBA transitions, the 95% usage interval widens further to 10.1%-27.4%.

Players who make this move typically sit only 0.46 sd above their own league's average, well below this subject's 0.92 sd standing, and the fitted translation slopes (0.579 for usage, 0.751 for true shooting) mean even a strong source profile only partially carries over.

strengths.text: In the EuroLeague, the subject produced 21.636 points per 75 possessions on 65.3% true shooting, a mark 1.01 standard deviations above the league's own true shooting average.
The subject carried a well above-average offensive role, with a usage rate of 24.9% (+0.92 sd within the EuroLeague), supported by a 12.4% assist rate and a low 6.9% turnover rate.
Rebounding production was strong at 8.433 per 75 possessions, with 42.9% of shot attempts coming from three-point range, indicating a stretch skill set.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate spans 13.1% to 24.4%, more than double the receiving league's usage standard deviation of 5.6%, so the model can rank this player against peers but cannot pin down an individual number. The true shooting projection of 58.4% should not be trusted at all: the model's out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league-mean baseline (4.7%).
